messages.subject: Using inputs created from javascript
parts:
My example app can be seen here: http://spark.rstudio.com/jazz12man/drag_drop/

The goal is to take the inputs selected from selectInputs(), add them as spans to a div with the ID "unassigned", and then assign the values to either "group1" or "group2". I then want to create output designating what values have been added to group1 and to group, and this is where I run into problems. It seems to work when I use HTML() in server.R to define the output to create divs with the output ID tag, but not when I use input$inputId 

I thought that I was returning text values, and that it should work similarly to how textarea works: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14452465/how-to-create-textarea-as-input-in-a-shiny-webapp-in-r

Any idea of what is going on? Any help would be greatly appreciated!


ui.R
alanOutput = function(outputId) {
  div(id=outputId, class="shiny-alan-output")
}
# ui shiny practice dragdrop
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(  
  headerPanel("",
              tags$head(
                tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="dragDrop.css"),
                tags$script(src="dragDrop.js")
              )
  ),
  
  sidebarPanel(
    h3("Select Items to add to list"),
    selectInput("additemstolist","(Hold 'ctrl' to select multiple items)",
                paste("Input to Server",1:10),selected=NULL,multiple=T),
    tags$style(type="text/css","#additemstolist {height: 200px}")
  ),
  
  mainPanel(
    
    htmlOutput("try3"),
    tags$p(style="padding-bottom: 200px;"),
    tags$hr(),
    h5("Unassigned"),
    htmlOutput("result_unass"),
    h5("group1"),
    htmlOutput("result_g1"),
    h5("group2"),
    htmlOutput("result_g2")
    
  )
))

server.R
values = paste("List Value",1:10)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {  
  output$try3 = renderText({
    c('
      <section id="user-levels">
      <div id="unassigned" ondrop="dropUser(this, event)" ondragenter="return false" ondragover="return false">
      Unassigned',
      paste('<span draggable="true" class="user" id="',
            tolower(gsub(" ","_",input$additemstolist)),'" ondragstart="dragUser(this, event)">',
            input$additemstolist,
            '</span>'),
      '</div>
      <div id="group1" ondrop="dropUser(this, event)" ondragenter="return
      false" ondragover="return false">
      <em>Group 1</em>
      </div>
      <div id="group2" ondrop="dropUser(this, event)" ondragenter="return false"
      ondragover="return false">
      <em>Group 2</em>
      </div>
      </section>
      ')
  })
  
  observe({
    cat(input$group1_update)
  })
  
  output$results_unass = renderPrint({
    input$result_unass
  })
  
  output$result_g1 = renderText({
    paste0(input$group1_update,collapse="|")
  })
  
  output$result_g2 = renderText({
    HTML('<div id="group2_update"></div>')
  })
  
})
  

.js
function dragUser(user, event) {
  event.dataTransfer.setData('User', user.id);
}
function dropUser(target, event) {
  var user = event.dataTransfer.getData('User');
  target.appendChild(document.getElementById(user));
  var g1 = $.map($("#group1 span"), function(elem, index){
    return $(elem).html();
  });
  var g2 = $.map($("#group2 span"), function(elem, index){
    return $(elem).html();
  });
  var unass = $.map($("#unassigned span"), function(elem, index){
    return $(elem).html();
  });
   $("#group1_update").text(g1);
  $("#group2_update").text(g2);
  $("#unass_update").text(unass);
}

.css
#user-levels {
  width: 900px;
  margin: 0 auto;
}
#group1, #group2, #unassigned {
float: left;
width: 202px;
height: 170px;
padding: 5px 10px;
margin-right: 3px;
background: #eee;
text-align: center;
}
.user {
width: 130px;
padding: 0 5px;
display: block;
margin: 0 auto 3px;
  border-radius: 10px;
text-align: center;
border: 1px solid #aaa;
background: #ddd;
  box-shadow: 3px 3px 3px #ccc;
/*cursor: pointer;*/
}
.user:hover {
    cursor: pointer;
    border: 2px solid #aaa;
    /*border-radius: 2px;*/
}

messages.subject: Re: Using inputs created from javascript
parts:
Looking at your code I think you know Javascript, DOM and etc so I hope my explanation will make sense.

Pro-Shiny users please correct me if I am wrong.

  • For your input$group1_update to work you need a DOM element that can be retrieved with 
    • scope = document; $(scope).find("#group1_update") as soon as the DOM is ready. This is related to your find function.
    • $("#group2_update") return an element though. I suspect you actually want a more general $(scope).(".alanBinding") in your code
  • you need to tell Shiny that the values you wanted from input$group1_update has been updated. This is done in the subscribe function
    • currently Shiny knows that your input has been updated if the change event happened on an element that you obtain from the find function with class = alanBinding
      • see your subscribe function
    • But your find function returns an element with id = "group1_inpout" and this element does not exists and has no class called alanBinding
So I suspect that including div(id = "group1_input", class = "alanBinding" ..... ) in your ui.R might be what you need to get you started.

I believe Shiny will query the document looking for shiny objects once the DOM is ready. This is done with the find function. In the your code you defined the find function as

find: function(scope) {
    return $(scope).find("#group1_update");
  },

Once the DOM is ready I think Shiny will use the document object as the scope and use the find function to identify all alanBinding inputs elements. So it is running $(document).find("#group1_update") to try and find your object. So it returns null. So Shiny thinks there is no input object of type alanBinding 

Also maybe   
find: function(scope) {
    return $(scope).find(".alanBinding");
  }
is what you actually wanted. But then you need to make sure that the element with id group1_input has the class alanBinding
